title: Captive demand is the dominant revealed US debt strategy
statement: Treasury funds the deficit with bills and uses rules (eSLR, GENIUS reserve rules, FIMA, buybacks) to create buyers for them. The pattern is confirmed, whether it is a design or the default path is still open.

evidence.text: Nominal coupon sizes frozen, guidance 'for at least the next several quarters'. Treasury 'is monitoring SOMA purchases of Treasury bills and growing demand for Treasury bills from the private sector'
Bills 22.36% of marketable debt ($7.118T), up from 21.53% a year earlier
Net bill supply up more than $550B in Jul-Aug 2026, money funds absorbed about 85%. Stablecoins hold nearly $200B of bills and short Treasuries. Bank holdings up more than $300B since end 2024
GENIUS reserves limited to cash, deposits, Treasuries of 93 days or less and bill repo

Bessent: 'Just as President Abraham Lincoln's National Currency Act of 1863 established a national framework for bank-issued currency, the GENIUS Act establishes a federal framework for payment stablecoins'
Long-end buybacks raised to at least $4B per operation, ran at $6B. $230B of buybacks in 2026

mechanism: $2T deficit with coupons frozen means bills fill the gap
Rules route demand to bills: money funds, bank portfolios (eSLR), stablecoins (93-day rule), Fed bill purchases
Treasury buys back long bonds, so the public holds less duration
Japan kept from selling via signals and FIMA
Term premium contained at the margin, but interest now resets with the policy rate
falsifier: The 4 Nov 2026 refunding raises coupon sizes materially and drops the 'several quarters' guidance, or the bill share falls below 21%.
dissent: Short issuance is simply the default for a large deficit with 10y yields above 5%. Bessent also wants banks to hold fewer safe assets, and TBAC expects coupon increases in FY2027.

views.governance: Debt management is now done through regulation, which hides its cost and ties federal interest to every Fed hike.
views.business: Front-end Treasury paper has a structural bid, the long end does not. Expect more bill-like products.
views.uhi_citizen: Cash in money funds and stablecoins is financing the deficit. The stablecoin version pays the holder nothing.

title: Stablecoins as the petrodollar of the 2020s
statement: In function, dollar stablecoins recycle foreign savers' demand into Treasury bills like petrodollars did. At today's size (4.3% of bills, under 1% of debt) they do not matter for the debt. They could by H1 if supply reaches $1T to $3T.

evidence.text: Total stablecoins about $301B, USDT about 61% share, USAT about $183M
Stablecoins total $305B = 4.3% of $7.12T bills. Tether direct bills 1.6% of bills
Fed staff interquartile range of private estimates: $1T to $3T of stablecoins by end of decade
TBAC median dealer forecast implies a $1.45T funding shortfall in FY2027-28 at current coupon sizes
Collins (Tether co-founder): stablecoins are 'one extra customer buying a couple hundred billion dollars of treasuries'
RBI Deputy Governor: stablecoins 'would reduce demand for the local currency and raise the risk of dollarisation'

mechanism: Foreign savers swap weak local currency for dollar tokens
Issuers must hold bills, bill repo or deposits
New front-end demand lets Treasury tilt issuance to bills
Seigniorage moves from weak-currency countries to US issuers and the Treasury
Gross holdings overstate net new demand when dollars come from US money funds or bank deposits
falsifier: Supply stays below $500B through end 2028, or compliant tokens fail to displace offshore USDT after the 2028-07-18 DASP ban.

tripwires.meaning: comparable to a major buyer class

dissent: Supply stalled near $320B since May 2026 despite GENIUS, and much of the growth just moves dollars from money funds, so net new Treasury demand is small.

views.governance: Weak-currency governments face currency substitution and lost seigniorage, expect capital controls or CBDCs in response.
views.business: The float income is the business model, the yield ban makes issuance a toll booth.
views.uhi_citizen: Good for cheap payments and remittances, a poor savings vehicle because it pays no yield.

title: US private rails vs China public CBDC
statement: The US banned a retail CBDC to 2030 and licensed private bill-backed stablecoins, while China keeps digital money public and blocks private RMB tokens. The US turns digital dollar demand into Treasury demand while keeping control through freeze rules and Fed settlement.

evidence.text: H.R. 6644 law 2026-07-11: the Fed 'may not issue or create a central bank digital currency' through 2030-12-31, private permissionless dollar tokens exempt
GENIUS Act signed 2025-07-18, effective 2027-01-18. OCC final rule issued 2026-10-21
PBoC ordered stablecoin crackdown (Nov 2025). Reported CSRC ban on RMB stablecoins (Feb 2026, single source)
Kraken limited Fed master account, no discount window, no interest on reserves

mechanism: CBDC ban reserves the retail digital dollar for private issuers
Private issuers must hold Treasuries, so digital dollar growth equals bill demand
FinCEN/OFAC freeze obligations keep state control
Fed keeps final settlement via payment accounts
China keeps data and capital controls but limits e-CNY reach outside state deals
falsifier: The US repeals the ban and launches a retail CBDC, or China licenses an offshore CNH stablecoin at scale.
dissent: The ban is temporary and passed on a housing bill without the President's signature, so it could flip in a crisis, and stablecoin rails are permissioned enough to look like a CBDC run by banks.

views.governance: Two digital blocs: US private dollar apps that reach individuals directly versus state rails negotiated government to government.
views.business: Build on licensed dollar rails and expect freeze and KYC obligations.
views.uhi_citizen: Private issuance does not mean private or unsurveilled money.

title: Gold as the neutral reserve layer, mostly by price
statement: Central banks keep buying gold as a no-counterparty reserve between nations, but its jump in reserve share is mostly price, buying is lumpy and price-sensitive, and some preachers (Russia) are sellers.

evidence.text: Q2 2026 net official buying 289t, Q1 57t, H1 345t lowest since 2022. Russia -22t largest seller. Poland +51t, China +33t
ECB: at end-2025 prices gold 27% of official reserves, Treasuries 22%, euro 15%. At end-2023 prices gold would be about 16%
France withdrew all 129t of its gold from the NY Fed (Jul 2025 to Jan 2026)
US gold still booked at $42.2222/oz, 261.5M oz, $11.04B book

mechanism: Sanctions risk on dollar and euro custody rises
Reserve managers buy gold and repatriate custody
Buying is value-driven, heavier when price falls
Share rises mostly by price, tonnage grows slowly
Gold settles trust between states, not daily commerce
falsifier: Two or more consecutive quarters of net official selling, or the gold reserve share falls back below 20% at constant prices.

tripwires.threshold: another G20 member repatriates from NY

dissent: A few large buyers (China, Poland) drive the totals, and the largest rhetorical champion (Russia) is selling, so this may be concentrated hedging rather than a system-wide layer.

views.governance: Gold custody location is now a sovereignty choice, expect more repatriation and less use of New York and London vaults.
views.business: Gold is a reserve hedge and collateral of last resort, not a payment rail. Tokenized gold has struggled.
views.uhi_citizen: Gold protects against the system failing, not inside the daily payment system.

title: Bitcoin in H0: politically blessed risk asset, not a reserve asset
statement: The US holds forfeited bitcoin but buys none, plans no revaluation and bars borrowing to buy, and collateral use is tiny. In H0 bitcoin is a risk asset with political status and a frozen sovereign stockpile.

evidence.text: No federal purchases. Witt (2026-10-14): priority is safeguarding and accounting, no purchase strategy, buying needs Congress
ARMA (H.R. 8957) reported 28-21: 20-year hold, no acquisition authority, bars borrowing, new taxes, pledging federal assets
Crypto-collateralised lending $56.16B (Q2 2026), down from $78.69B peak

mechanism: EO and ARMA freeze forfeited BTC (198k-328k coins, about $17-28B)
No buying and a 20-year hold remove supply without adding sovereign demand
Price trades with liquidity and real rates
Live monetary niches are sanctions zones and weak-currency savers
falsifier: A federal bitcoin purchase, budget-neutral acquisition via gold revaluation or ESF, or a G20 central bank disclosing a BTC reserve.

tripwires.indicator: US government BTC wallet inflows from market purchases

dissent: Bitcoin rose while gold fell in mid-2026 and Russia legalized it for trade, so its neutral-money role may be growing outside the official sector faster than the data shows.

views.governance: Bitcoin has political status without balance-sheet status, the stockpile is a sanctions and forfeiture ledger.
views.business: Treat BTC as a volatile risk asset, not reserve collateral.
views.uhi_citizen: Size bitcoin as a speculation, not as savings that replaces cash or gold.

title: Bessent 'sold France to help Japan' (literal)
statement: The claim that the US euro sale was a plan to break France and solve the US debt is refuted on size, timing and outcome.

evidence.text: ESF: yen holdings +$500M, euro holdings -$500M, operations 2026-07-31 settled 2026-08-05
Japan bought ¥15.3993tn (about $97B) from 30 Jul to 26 Aug
OAT-Bund 10y spread 78bp (Jul avg), 82bp (Aug avg), 87bp (10 Sep), 157.5bp (21 Oct)
Germany trade surplus €146.0B Jan-Aug 2026 vs €140.4B. Bund flat as haven

mechanism: Claimed: US sells euros, pushes adjustment onto the euro
Claimed: Japan sells Europe, France cracks
Claimed: safe-haven money lowers US yields, dollar then devalued
Observed: $500M is too small, spread lagged six weeks with other causes, US yields and dollar rose
falsifier: NY Fed Q3 FX report or ESF statements show a multi-billion or repeated euro sale, or documents show US-Japan agreement to route Japanese selling to the euro area.

tripwires.indicator: NY Fed Q3 FX operations report
tripwires.threshold: US leg above $5B or repeated euro sales
stabilize while OAT holdings fall sharply

dissent: Signals, not money, were the instrument, and the US did choose to make the euro the funding currency without telling the ECB.

views.governance: Treat it as a convention break (no ECB notice), not an attack.
views.business: The short-France, short-EUR/JPY trade is crowded and already priced.
views.uhi_citizen: No direct effect outside France, the bigger driver is the oil shock and rate hikes.

title: Narrow version: the euro area as the chosen shock absorber
statement: The US chose a funding currency (euros) and a policy mix (pressing BoJ hikes, FIMA instead of Treasury sales) that pushed the cost of yen defence and Japanese portfolio rotation away from the dollar and Treasuries toward the euro area, where France is the most exposed link. Bessent welcomes the resulting flows. Intent to harm France is not shown.

evidence.text: ESF sold euros, not dollars, for yen, ECB not told in advance
Bessent urged Fed to upsize FIMA, Japan MoF 'plans to use' FIMA
Bessent on 20 Oct: 'money flow out of some countries of concern and into US Treasuries'
Allianz: France 'first victim of the Japanese repatriation trade', Japanese hold about 5% of OATs
Counter: Japanese net bought OATs Jun-Aug, AFT head says no Japanese selling seen, non-resident share 58.4% end-June

mechanism: US avoids selling dollars or Treasuries
Japan pushed toward FIMA and higher domestic rates
Japanese investors rotate out of their most overweight, riskiest foreign holding
France absorbs part of the adjustment
Haven flows reach Treasuries at the margin
falsifier: Disclosure that the euro choice was purely operational (euros were the ESF's largest liquid asset) and the OAT spread compresses toward 80-100bp after the budget passes with no change in Japanese flows.
dissent: France's spread is explained by its own budget, politics and the global term premium, and Japan's official sector sold Treasuries heavily anyway.

views.governance: Europe should expect to absorb adjustment when the US and Japan manage the yen, a reason to finish the digital euro and a backstop.
views.business: Euro-area weak links carry a new exposure to Japanese flows.
views.uhi_citizen: French savers and banks bear the cost through higher rates and weaker bank shares.

title: Mar-a-Lago in practice: selective, not broad devaluation
statement: In 2026 the US is weakening the dollar only against Asian surplus currencies (yen, yuan) through bilateral pressure, while the broad dollar rose. A broad devaluation needs Fed easing and is unlikely before 2027-28.

evidence.text: US joint yen intervention, Bessent: yen 'substantially undervalued'
USD/CNY 6.67, yuan +6.35% y/y, strongest since mid-2022
DXY +2.8% y/y
Century bonds and foreign-holder user fees absent from refunding statements
Bessent: dollar benefits 'are no longer unconditional'

mechanism: Tariffs and FX monitoring create leverage
Partners strengthen their own currencies (Japan intervenes, PBoC fixes stronger)
US avoids selling dollars
Fed hiking keeps the broad dollar firm
Broad weakening waits for Fed personnel change or a crisis
falsifier: PBoC reverses to weaken the yuan and the US declines the next joint operation, or a broad DXY fall below 97 with Fed cuts and a formal accord.
dissent: Plaza (1985) also started with a strong dollar, and a quiet US-China currency bargain may already be in place, so a broad move could come faster than the Fed path suggests.

views.governance: Currency policy is now bilateral pressure tied to trade and security, not G7 communiques.
views.business: Asian currency strength is policy-backed, hedge imported-input costs.
views.uhi_citizen: Goods imported from Asia get dearer at the margin.

title: Fiscal path: managed repression is the likeliest exit
statement: Today the US relies on captive demand plus passive inflation (nominal growth above the average debt cost) plus hope for AI growth. As the debt reprices, the likeliest H1 exit is managed financial repression, not AI salvation or default.

evidence.text: Average rate on marketable debt 3.518%
FY2026 net interest $1,051.8B vs defense $965.2B, 19.5% of receipts
10y real yield 2.76% (from 1.94%), breakeven about 2.37%
70% of marketable debt reprices within 5 years. Interest to about $1.6T in 3 years and $1.9T in 5 if yields hold (L7 model)
FOMC hiked 12-0 to 3.75-4.00%, Warsh: QE 'sparingly, if at all'

mechanism: Effective rate 3.2% vs nominal growth 5.7% erodes the ratio about 2.5pp a year
Primary deficit 2.9% of GDP offsets most of that
Repricing closes the gap within five years
Pressure builds on the Fed to tolerate inflation or cap yields
Fed leadership turnover after 2028 makes repression feasible
falsifier: The primary deficit falls toward balance, or inflation drops to 2% while real yields fall, or real growth runs above 3.5% for several years with flat real rates.

tripwires.threshold: breakeven above 2.75% with real yields falling

dissent: Warsh's Fed is hiking against the President, and if inflation falls with high real rates the ratio climbs faster, forcing fiscal action instead of repression.

views.governance: Repression is the politically cheapest exit but needs a cooperative Fed, so Fed independence is the key institutional battleground.
views.business: Own real assets and pricing power, avoid long fixed-rate claims.
views.uhi_citizen: Fixed incomes and savings lose purchasing power quietly, wages and benefits must be indexed.

title: Scenario probabilities S1 to S4 by horizon
statement: Dominant regime at the end of each horizon: dollar extension leads in H0 and H1, while a neutral reserve layer and a disorderly reset gain weight over time. An energy or compute standard stays a small probability until H2.
scenario_reasoning: Main table: which scenario best describes the system at the end of the horizon, so rows sum to 100. Scenarios coexist (S1 plumbing can carry S4 repression, gold can grow under S1), so a second table gives the chance each element is materially present at all. H0 S1 is high because all binding law points to private dollar rails and the dollar is up. H0 S4 is 22 because of the oil shock, 5%+ yields, a shrinking official holder base and bill-heavy funding. H1 adds the CBDC-ban sunset, the 2028 offshore-stablecoin ban, repricing of 70% of debt and Fed turnover. H2 spreads probability, with S3 at 10 because any energy unit needs a scarcity rule.

evidence.text: GENIUS effective 2027-01-18, OCC final rule
CBDC ban through 2030-12-31
Foreign official Treasury holdings -$254B Feb-Aug 2026
Official gold buying 289t in Q2 2026
A fixed-kWh unit is inflationary while energy costs fall (solar learning rate about 28%)

mechanism: S1 grows through H0 on law already enacted
A repression episode (S4-lite) in late H0 or H1 runs partly through S1 plumbing
Gold's neutral role expands underneath
Bitcoin stays private and sanctions-zone unless a G20 central bank breaks ranks
S3 only if machine economies grow large and adopt a scarcity-ruled unit
falsifier: By 2028: stablecoins below $500B and dollar reserve share below 50% (S1 down), or official gold net selling (S2 down), or 10y above 6% with Fed yield control (S4 up).

tripwires.meaning: S1 down, S2 or S4 up

dissent: Probabilities beyond 2035 are judgment, not measurement, and the base rate of reserve-system change after a crisis argues S4 could be higher in H1.

views.governance: Plan for S1 as base case but build S4 contingencies (yield control rules, FIMA capacity, gold custody).
views.business: Hold dollar liquidity on licensed rails, plus some neutral reserve exposure.
views.uhi_citizen: Expect dollars to stay the daily money, protect savings against a repression episode.

title: The merger is an acquisition: one dollar board with a gold corner
statement: Set 1 and Set 2 are merging, but Set 1 is absorbing Set 2: dollar stablecoins are tokenized bill funds, tokenized Treasuries settle in DTC, crypto firms get Fed access without bank privileges, bitcoin is frozen, and gold sits in the corner as the neutral asset between nations.

board.bank_settlement: Federal Reserve: reserves and Fedwire, payment accounts for crypto firms without interest on reserves or discount window
board.backing: Short Treasuries (93 days or less), bill repo, bank deposits. Gold and BTC only at offshore issuers like Tether
board.issuers: Federally permitted issuers: bank subsidiaries, licensed firms (Circle, Paxos, USAT), tokenized deposits. Offshore only via Treasury comparability
board.rails: Public and permissioned blockchains for retail and AI-agent payments, tokenized securities settling back into DTC/NSCC
board.toll_booths: Issuers (float yield, holders get none), exchanges (rewards), custodians (BNY, Anchorage, Cantor), compliance freeze points (FinCEN/OFAC), Treasury (cheaper bills), Fed (access)
board.neutral_corner: Physical gold in domestic custody between nations
board.jail: Secondary sanctions covering banking, digital assets and gold
board.rival_boards: China e-CNY, CIPS, gold. EU MiCA plus digital euro around 2029

evidence.text: GENIUS reserve rule and 2028 ban on non-permitted stablecoins for US persons
DTC tokenization pilot includes Treasuries, Nasdaq tokenized shares settle via NSCC/DTC
Tether reserves: T-bills $114.96B, gold 146.2t, BTC 98,933, against USDT $184.6B
Tokenized Treasuries about $14.7B to $15.4B, two thirds held outside the US
Bessent: GENIUS like the 1863 National Currency Act

mechanism: Law makes every compliant token a holder of short Treasuries
Settlement stays at the Fed and DTC
Licences create a small set of toll collectors
Sanctions decide who may sit at the board
Nations that distrust the board hold gold in their own vaults
falsifier: Offshore stablecoins keep a majority share after 2028-07-18, or a non-dollar token (gold, BTC or compute unit) gains material share in machine commerce by 2035.

tripwires.threshold: finding for Tether's home regime or reciprocity deal

tripwires.meaning: machine commerce on the dollar board

dissent: Offshore USDT, partly backed by gold and bitcoin, and China's public rails form a second board the US does not control, so the merger may be only half done.

views.governance: Treasury and the Fed write the board's rules, sanctions access is the enforcement tool, and the 2030 CBDC sunset is the next decision point.
views.business: The scarce assets are licences: issuance, custody, compliance and Fed access.
views.uhi_citizen: Payments get cheaper and faster, but the yield on your money goes to the issuer, and access can be frozen.

title: Bitcoin as a future neutral reserve between nations
statement: Bitcoin could join gold as a neutral reserve between nations in H2, but no central bank buying is confirmed and sanctions now target digital assets.

evidence.text: Putin (Dec 2024): 'bitcoin, who can prohibit it? No one'
Russia legalized crypto trading, CBR says BTC, ETH and USDT qualify
Operation Economic Outcast adds secondary sanctions on digital assets and gold
US spot ETFs hold about 1.293M BTC

mechanism: Sanctions push states toward counterparty-free assets
Gold already fills the role
Bitcoin enters only if a G20 central bank breaks ranks
Volatility and sanctions targeting slow adoption
falsifier: No G20 central bank discloses a bitcoin reserve by 2035.
dissent: Fixed supply and no counterparty make bitcoin the natural digital twin of gold once custody and volatility improve.

views.governance: Watch sanctioned and swing states first.
views.uhi_citizen: Do not plan savings around a sovereign bitcoin bid.

title: Holder-base shift: official buyers out, leveraged private in
statement: Foreign official holders are shrinking their Treasuries while custodial and leveraged holders replace them, which makes the market more price-sensitive and explains why Treasury builds captive demand.

evidence.text: Foreign official holdings $4,009.6B (Feb) to $3,755.6B (Aug 2026). Japan -$171B, China -$104B, UK above $1T
NY Fed foreign official custody $2.549T, -$202B y/y

mechanism: Official holders sell to defend currencies or diversify
Basis traders, money funds and stablecoins replace them
Marginal buyer becomes price-sensitive and leveraged
Funding shocks transmit faster into yields
dissent: Part of the fall is valuation from higher yields and Japan's sales funded intervention, not a strategic exit.

views.governance: Fragility rises, so FIMA and standing repo capacity matter more.
views.business: Expect more volatility in Treasury yields and basis spreads.
views.uhi_citizen: Mortgage and loan rates can jump on funding shocks.
